paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus comes to His people in the middle of the storm. The disciples were far from land, with the wind against them, and Jesus was already on His way to them (Matthew 14:24-25). When they cried out in fear, He spoke up at once: "Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid." (Matthew 14:27). He doesn't wait for your boat to quit rocking before He shows up.

Now look at Peter, because Peter is every one of us. He walked on the water for real, and then he saw the strength of the wind and began to sink (Matthew 14:29-30). I think the lesson is that faith keeps its eyes on Jesus, because the wind is LOUD and it never runs out of things to say. But notice what happens when Peter cries out, "Lord, save me!" Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of him (Matthew 14:30-31). I've sunk in a bowl of chocolate chips on a good day, so trust me, the grip matters more than the balance.

So what do you do on your own stormy night? You call out to Him, and you keep your eyes on Him. At the end, those in the boat worshiped Jesus, saying, "Truly You are the Son of God!" (Matthew 14:33). The people of Gennesaret figured it out too, and all who touched Him were healed (Matthew 14:36). Jesus is who He says He is, so bring Him your waves, friend, and bring Him your fear.
